req.title: Reject empty firstName
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the Player payload contains an empty firstName.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the system should reject a Player payload with an empty firstName by returning an HTTP 422 status code. This ensures data integrity by preventing incomplete player records from being created. The test suite includes a positive test to verify correct behavior with valid input, a negative test to check the rejection of invalid input, and a boundary test to ensure robustness around the edge case of an empty firstName.

tests.name: test_create_player_with_valid_first_name
preconditions: The database is pre-loaded with valid player data.
actions: Send a POST request to /players/ with a valid firstName.
expected: The response contains the created player data.
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

valid_player = {
    "firstName": "John",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "squadNumber": 27,
    "position": "Forward"
}

response = client.post("/players/", json=valid_player)
assert response.status_code == 201
assert response.json()["firstName"] == "John"
assert response.json()["lastName"] == "Doe"

tests.name: test_create_player_with_empty_first_name
preconditions: The database is pre-loaded with valid player data.
actions: Send a POST request to /players/ with an empty firstName.
expected: The response contains an error message indicating validation failure.
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

invalid_player = {
    "firstName": "",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "squadNumber": 28,
    "position": "Forward"
}

response = client.post("/players/", json=invalid_player)
assert response.status_code == 422
assert "Unprocessable Entity" in response.json()["detail"]
